top.title: Cowboys Skip Deadline Splashes To Bet On Existing Talent
top.description: Robert Goddin-Imagn Images The Dallas Cowboys stayed quiet at the trade deadline. While other teams scrambled for last-minute upgrades, Dallas decided to trust the players already in the building. ESPN insider Adam Schefter noted that the organization never appeared close to making another major deal. “It never sounded like they got close to making any big deals,” Schefter said, adding that there was no real movement on a George Pickens trade. This approach puts the pressure squarely on the current squad to deliver results over the final eight games. Why The Roster Stays Put General Manager Jerry Jones and the front office clearly believe they have enough pieces to win. They already spent a 2028 second-round pick earlier in the season to add cornerback Joey Porter Jr. from the Pittsburgh Steelers. That move gave the secondary a physical presence without burning up all their draft capital. The team said the addition was an aggressive upgrade to the roster. “Rather than surrender more draft capital, the organization will give its existing players an opportunity to deliver,” the report states. In the last game on Sunday, Nov. 8, Prescott threw for 335 yards and two touchdowns against Indianapolis. CeeDee Lamb caught 10 passes for 195 yards, proving he can dominate when given the ball. Javonte Williams also ran for 101 yards and a score, showing the run game can keep defenses honest. However, the defense faces a much harder test in the next matchup. In his last four games, Quinnen Williams has recorded 10 tackles for loss and four sacks, marking a recent standout performance. The Challenge Looming Sunday San Francisco enters the stadium on Sunday, Nov. 15, with a 7-1 record and a six-game winning streak. They are not just a good team; they have beaten Dallas in their last four meetings, including two playoff games. The 49ers added Keenan Allen to their squad before the deadline for a 2027 sixth-round pick. His arrival adds another layer of difficulty for a Cowboys defense that needs to limit explosive plays. Dallas coach Brian Schottenheimer admitted that tight end Jake Ferguson and running back Tyler Goodson will miss multiple weeks due to knee injuries. “A lot of these guys, they play on adrenaline,” Schottenheimer said, highlighting the team’s resilience despite these setbacks, according to WJOX-FM . They need consistent performances to keep their playoff hopes alive. “The Cowboys still believe they have the talent they need to make a late second half of the season push here,” Schefter added. The next game starts at 4:25 p.m. ET on Sunday, Nov. 15, at AT&T Stadium when the San Francisco 49ers visit the Dallas Cowboys.

top.title: England's Mitchell could miss Six Nations after hamstring operation
top.description: Mitchell's four hamstring injuries this year have not all been on the same leg, with three to his right and one to his left [Getty Images] England scrum-half Alex Mitchell could miss next year's Six Nations after an operation to fix recurring hamstring issues. The 29-year-old, who was Steve Borthwick's first-choice nine last season, has gone under the knife after suffering four hamstring injuries this year. If Mitchell, who has recovered ahead of schedule in the past, follows an estimated four-month rehabilitation it would give him a chance of playing in England's final two matches, against Wales and Scotland on 6 and 13 March. Any setback however would leave him with only pre-tournament friendlies to play in for England before next year's Rugby World Cup in Australia. Mitchell's latest hamstring injury, which came in Northampton's win over Gloucester last month, ruled him out of this month's Nations Championship campaign. Mitchell suffered an injury to the same hamstring against Ireland in February and again against Fiji in July. He also tweaked his other hamstring - his left, non-kicking leg - in an England training camp in May. Mitchell told the i Paper last month that he had been given the option, like skipper Maro Itoje, to skip England's summer fixtures against South Africa, Fiji and Argentina, but opted to play instead. While Jack van Poortvliet has emerged as Borthwick's starting pick in Mitchell's absence, there is competition behind the Leicester man with Bristol's Harry Randall, Bath's Ben Spencer and Mitchell's club team-mate Archie McParland all vying for position. Mitchell travelled to Finland to be operated on by Lasse Lempainen, a specialist in elite sporting injuries. Chelsea and England defender Reece James and Paris St-Germain's Ballon D'Or winner Ousmane Dembele are among Lempainen's previous patients, both returning to consistent playing time after a string of muscular injuries. Mitchell's England team-mate Ben Curry was also operated on by Lempainen and has made a successful return to action after 10 months out, featuring in England's win over Australia last weekend. top.title: Ghana kick-start Afcon 2027 bid despite Ayew penalty miss
top.description: Jordan Ayew joined Championship side Sheffield United in September after spending two seasons with Leicester City [Getty Images] Ghana belatedly kick-started their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) qualifying campaign with a 2-0 home win over Somalia. The Black Stars had lost their opening two Group C matches against Ivory Coast and The Gambia, leading to the departure of coach Carlos Queiroz by mutual consent. Ghana women's coach Kim Bjorkegren was placed in interim charge for this month's double-header against the Ocean Stars, with the West Africans in danger of missing a second successive edition of the Afcon finals. The hosts were given a chance to take an early lead in Sekondi-Takoradi after Alidu Seidu was pulled down in the box, but Jordan Ayew's 14th-minute penalty was saved by Somalia goalkeeper Ibrahim Hussein. Ghana did go ahead in first-half stoppage time when Mohammed Salisu headed Mohammed Kudus's deep corner back across goal and Jonas Adjetey nodded in from six yards out. Felix Afena-Gyan doubled the Black Stars' advantage just after the hour mark when his shot from inside the box squirmed under Hussein and over the line. The result puts the four-time continental champions three points behind Ivory Coast and The Gambia, who meet in Bouake at 19:00 GMT. Cameroon, DR Congo and Senegal are also in action among seven other Afcon 2027 qualifiers on Thursday.

top.title: Alysa Liu speaks on new winning mentality in Life magazine cover story
top.description: This winter, Alysa Liu was the name on everyone's lips. The skating star, who hails from Oakland, wowed audiences around the world when she won the individual gold medal at the 2026 Winter Olympics in Milan . She also won the group gold with Team USA. The then-20-year-old captured attention with her confidence in her individuality, including a striped hairstyle and a "smiley" piercing. She is now taking a break and is not competing in the 2026-27 season , but promises "I have a plan" in her cover story for LIFE Magazine that was published online Thursday, Nov. 12. The publication will return to print on Nov. 23, which is 90 years after its first issue. The comeback arrives after a nearly 20-year hiatus. Liu is the first of five cover stars that will be featured on the first edition of the re-upped quarterly magazine. The story, written by Bonnie Tsui, is accompanied by striking photographs by Spike Jonze of Liu skating in a flowing red outfit in a darkened rink. The feature reflects on Liu's previous time stepping away from the sport during the COVID pandemic. She realized that she wasn't skating for herself, but to please others. "When I was younger, I wanted to win all the time," she said. "But winning was really about getting reassurance from my coach and my dad, and just making them happy, making them think I was, like, perfect or something." In the piece, Liu shows the many sides of her life after fame. She trains at the Yerba Buena Ice Skating & Bowling Center in San Francisco, carefully crafting her next routines with her coaches Phillip DiGuglielmo and Massimo Scali. She has a lunch full of laughs at A16, a pizzeria in Oakland, with her closest friends. Liu explained how her perspective in being open with the world has changed since rising to superstardom. She's not only become a sports icon, but has become a well-known name is fashion, attending the Met Gala and Paris Fashion Week. "I don’t really like hiding stuff about myself," she said. "But now, I low-key have to, to protect my peace." She pondered how taking ownership of her sport allowed her to travel with her siblings and makes her excited to support her United States teammates from the stands, emphasizing how she values camaraderie. Liu said at the peak of her unhappiness she "would cry all the time – like, every session – and not in a good way." But she has no regrets. "If I went back in time, I would still want myself to go through everything, just so I could come to my own conclusion," she said. "Now, I don’t look to other people to find my happiness anymore. That has changed the definition of winning for me." Fans can pre-order their copy of LIFE Magazine featuring Liu online or purchase a magazine at select retailers on Nov. 23. top.title: CJ McCollum joins NBA on Prime crew, discusses role on Hawks, Damian Lillard's comeback
top.description: CJ McCollum hit the game-winning shot in the Atlanta Hawks ' Game 3 victory over the New York Knicks in the first round of last year's playoffs. Not only does he remember that shot, but he remembers enjoying being a guest on Prime Video's "NBA Nightcap" postgame show where he appeared in his pajamas and the hosts joked he put the Knicks "to sleep." They all laughed about his role of villain as his son popped in to say hello. The party doesn't have to stop there as NBA on Prime announced on Thursday, Nov. 12 that the 14-year veteran guard will be a player commentator for several programs this season starting with "NBA Nightcap" on Friday, Nov. 13. "The conversation and team analysis that night was really fun," he told USA TODAY Sports of the postgame memories, "and I thought the chemistry was there, and I felt like it made a lot of sense (for me to join the Prime team). And I have a great appreciation for what NBA on Prime is doing, what the crew is doing, and how they educate and share authentic analysis." McCollum, 35, majored in journalism at Lehigh University and has experience hosting his own podcast with "The CJ McCollum Show" and "Pull Up with CJ McCollum." Among Prime's All-Star team of talent that he is joining is a mix of longtime broadcasters, including Kevin Harlan, and basketball greats like Udonis Haslem, Dirk Nowitzki, Steve Nash and Candace Parker. McCollum said the team is "a really cool atmosphere, really great environment of people that I respect and admire." "They're very honest. They watch the game. They're students of the game. They’re people who appreciate the game and they do a great job of describing why certain things are happening," he continued. "... When you have that group of professionals who have played the game, have talked the game, have lived the game, have been around it and seen it for so long, you get various impactful moments where viewers are able to really get a glimpse of what's actually happening, why it's happening, in an insightful way that they can digest." McCollum appreciates the craft of journalism and how showing the human element of any story brings people together. As journalism continues to face industry challenges , the 2016 Most Improved Player has hope. "Storytelling is vital. I think it makes the world a better place," he said. "Being able to hear people's stories, being able to see people's journeys not just in the sports world but in life, I think is something that we all can appreciate. "And journalism isn't dying. It's just evolving. But I think the people who move with integrity, who do things the right way and really appreciate the craft are continuing to thrive for sure." nigeria.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Independent National Electoral Commission INEC has begun deploying non-sensitive materials to the zones as it prepares for the 2027 general election. Acting Chairman of the commission, Prof. Rhoda Gumus, disclosed this on Thursday in Abuja at a benchmarking meeting with a delegation of Kenya’s Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission IEBC. “Right now, all non-sensitive materials are almost ready. In fact, today as we speak here, the non-sensitive materials have been lifted to some zones now,” Gumus said. She said the commission had completed nine of its scheduled activities and was preparing for the next phase. “We are preparing for the election next year and we have activities lined up. So far, we have been able to complete nine activities and we are still preparing for the next level of activities,” she said. Gumus said the commission’s leadership had just concluded a tour of the country’s six zones to assess their level of preparedness. “The purpose was to go round the zones to see how prepared we are, assess what the zones have put in place, their challenges and what to do. On Permanent Voter Cards PVCs, the acting chairman said production had been completed and distribution to the states was well advanced. “As of today, we can say that PVCs have been produced and the first, second batches, most of the states have received them. nigeria.title: Insecurity: Atiku tackles Tinubu as 638 are killed, 64,000 flee Nigeria
nigeria.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – Former Vice President and African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, has accused President Bola Tinubu of failing in his fundamental duty to protect Nigerians, following reports that 638 people were killed in insecurity-related incidents in October, while nearly 64,000 others fled violence in northern Nigeria to neighbouring Niger. The figures highlight the scale of the security crisis confronting the country, with Atiku demanding urgent action from the Federal Government to halt the killings, protect vulnerable communities and account for its efforts to restore public safety. In a statement by the Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Phrank Shaibu, Atiku described the figures as a devastating indictment of the country’s security situation. “Behind every number is a Nigerian whose life has been lost, a family in mourning or a community forced to abandon its home. Nigerians should not have to flee across our borders to find safety,” he said. The Centre for Democracy and Development’s October tracker recorded 638 deaths in broader insecurity incidents during the month, with the North-East accounting for 409. Across all security incidents, the figure stood at 640, up from 396 in September. The United Nations also reported that nearly 64,000 people had fled violence in northern Nigeria to Niger since the beginning of 2026, while several hundred others crossed into Benin. Calling for stronger security operations and support for displaced families, Atiku urged the Federal Government to work with neighbouring countries and humanitarian agencies to assist those forced to flee. “The Tinubu administration must make the protection of lives and communities its first responsibility. It must strengthen security in affected areas, support displaced families and work with neighbouring countries and humanitarian agencies to assist those who have fled. Nigerians also deserve a clear account of what is being done to stop the killings and restore safety,” he said. He challenged Tinubu to take responsibility for the worsening security situation rather than offer further explanations. “A government that cannot protect its people has failed in its most basic duty. President Tinubu must stop offering excuses and take responsibility for this worsening crisis. Nigerians need safety now, not another promise,” Atiku said. nigeria.title: Meet only two countries to have won both men’s and women’s FIFA World Cups
nigeria.description: Only two countries have won both the men’s and women’s FIFA World Cups, highlighting their achievements in international football across the men’s and women’s games. Germany and Spain are the only nations to have lifted both senior FIFA World Cup trophies since the women’s competition was introduced in 1991. While several countries have established themselves as dominant forces in either the men’s or women’s game, Germany and Spain have distinguished themselves by winning football’s biggest international prize in both categories. 1. Germany Germany became the first country to win both the men’s and women’s FIFA World Cups, establishing a record of success across the two competitions. The country’s men’s team has won the World Cup four times, in 1954, 1974, 1990 and 2014, making it one of the most successful national teams in the history of the tournament. Its first triumph came in 1954, when West Germany defeated Hungary 3-2 in the final in Switzerland, producing what became known as the ‘Miracle of Bern’. Germany subsequently won the competition in 1974 on home soil, defeating the Netherlands 2-1 in the final, before claiming a third title in 1990 with a 1-0 victory over Argentina in Italy. The country’s fourth triumph came in Brazil in 2014, when Mario Gotze scored the winning goal in extra time to secure a 1-0 victory over Argentina. Germany’s success has also extended to the women’s game, where the national team won consecutive FIFA Women’s World Cup titles in 2003 and 2007. In 2003, Germany defeated Sweden 2-1 after extra time in the final, with Nia Kunzer scoring the golden goal to deliver the country’s first women’s world title. Four years later, the team successfully defended its crown in China, defeating Brazil 2-0 in the final through goals from Birgit Prinz and Simone Laudehr. With four men’s titles and two women’s titles, Germany has won six senior FIFA World Cups combined, the highest total among countries to have won both competitions. 2. Spain Spain became the second country to achieve the double after winning the FIFA Women’s World Cup in 2023, joining Germany in the exclusive group. The country’s men’s team first conquered the world in 2010, when it defeated the Netherlands 1-0 after extra time in the final in South Africa. Andres Iniesta scored the decisive goal in the 116th minute, securing Spain’s maiden World Cup title under coach Vicente del Bosque. The triumph marked the culmination of a remarkable period for Spanish football, following the country’s victory at the 2008 European Championship. Thirteen years later, Spain’s women’s team delivered another historic achievement by winning its first FIFA Women’s World Cup. Spain defeated England 1-0 in the 2023 final in Sydney, Australia, with Olga Carmona scoring the decisive goal in the first half. Gemini declined to comment. A spokesperson for KAST would not discuss the transaction, but said the company is actively looking at acquisitions as its revenue and footprint grow. Neither firm has issued a public confirmation of a sale, and no regulator has announced a change-of-control approval. The disposal, if confirmed, would close a retreat Gemini laid out in February. On Feb. 4, the Nasdaq-listed company, known as Gemini (GEMI), approved a plan to exit and wind down its operations in the United Kingdom, the European Union and other European jurisdictions, and Australia, as part of a broader effort to cut expenses and support a path to profitability. It said it would keep operating in the United States and Singapore. The plan included a reduction in force of up to 200 employees in Europe, the United States and Singapore, or about 25% of Gemini’s global workforce as of that date. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine BNY Mellon Raises Its Strive (ASST) Stake 28% to $7 Million as Monday’s 13F Deadline Nears Bank of New York Mellon (BNY) raised its stake in Strive (ASST) by 28% in the third quarter, a Form 13F filed Nov. 5 shows, lifting the position to 237,100 shares worth $6.97 million at Sept. 30 prices. That is up 51,544 shares from the 185,556 BNY reported at June 30, when the same holding was valued at about $2.02 million. Most of the dollar jump is the stock. ASST’s implied price on the two filings rose from $10.91 at June 30 to $29.41 at Sept. 30, so the disclosed stake more than tripled in value even though the share count rose 28%. A 13F is a snapshot, not a trading diary. BNY filed a combination report that folds in holdings across its group, so the Strive line can include client, fund and discretionary positions rather than a single proprietary bet, and the firm may have changed the holding since Sept. 30. The bank oversees $63.4 trillion in assets under custody and/or administration and $2.2 trillion in assets under management, both as of Sept. 30. BNY held 1,056,230 shares of Strategy (MSTR) worth $161.7 million and 162,072 shares of BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) worth $7.67 million, a stake that nearly doubled from 85,282 shares at June 30 and is now about the same size as the Strive line. Monday’s deadline still has a few large filers outstanding Institutional managers that exercise investment discretion over $100 million or more in 13F securities have 45 days after quarter-end to disclose those holdings. That window ran to Nov. 14, a Saturday, so the deadline is Monday, Nov. 16. JPMorgan Chase filed its third-quarter 13F on Thursday. Wells Fargo, Millennium Management and Schonfeld Strategic Advisors had not appeared on the SEC’s EDGAR system as of Thursday morning. business.title: Rumble (RUM) Sells Two-Thirds of Its Bitcoin as AI Cloud Business Delivers First Profitable Quarter
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Rumble (RUM) Sells Two-Thirds of Its Bitcoin as AI Cloud Business Delivers First Profitable Quarter RUM Group, the parent of video platform Rumble, cut its bitcoin holdings by about two-thirds in the third quarter, the company disclosed Wednesday, as its newly acquired AI cloud business pushed it to its first profitable quarter on an adjusted basis. The Nasdaq-listed company held 94.68 bitcoin, valued at $7.9 million, as of Sept. 30. That compares with 293.14 bitcoin worth about $17.2 million at the end of June, according to its second-quarter results . That implies Rumble parted with roughly 198 bitcoin during the quarter, or about 68% of its stack. The company’s cash-flow statement shows a net sale of digital assets of about $15.3 million for the first nine months of 2026. In the same period a year earlier, it spent $19.1 million buying digital assets. Rumble did not explain the sales in its release, and it did not say what price it received. The balance sheet’s digital assets line, which the release does not break down, fell to $11.1 million from $18.5 million at the end of 2025. Revenue rose 290% from a year earlier to a record $96.6 million, beating the top of the company’s guidance range. Quake AI contributed $68.2 million of that, more than 70% of the total, in its first full quarter. The unit runs about 22,000 Nvidia GPUs, which the company said were about 85% utilized. Adjusted EBITDA came in at $4.4 million, the first positive result in company history. On a GAAP basis, RUM Group still lost $89.9 million, weighed down by $85.2 million in amortization and depreciation. Rumble’s video segment brought in $28.4 million, up 15% year over year, and posted a $12.1 million adjusted EBITDA loss, wider than a year earlier, executives said on the call. The company raised its stake in Northern Data to about 98% during the quarter and expects to own all of it in early 2027. It also warned that part of the roughly 250 megawatts of unmonetized capacity it had targeted for 2027 may slip beyond that year due to market conditions. Across the nine sessions since Oct. 30, IBIT has shed about $2 billion. The fund, the largest of the U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs, has seen money leave on every trading day so far in November. The broader group has fared only slightly better. The lone exception was Nov. 4, when $74.6 million came in, even as IBIT itself bled $201.2 million that day. IBIT accounts for about $1.77 billion of November’s outflows, or roughly 94% of the total. entertainment.description: Nigerian DJ and philanthropist Florence Otedola, popularly known as Cuppy, pictured wearing gold headphones and a camel-brown blazer. On her birthday, Florence Ifeoluwa Otedola is giving viewers a more personal glimpse into her life, exploring home, family, identity and purpose. For years, Nigerians have known Florence “Cuppy” Otedola as the internationally recognised DJ and philanthropist, often recognised by her signature pink hair and vibrant public personality. This birthday, however, her new documentary offers a closer look at the woman behind that familiar public image. Released on 11 November 2026, her new 12-minute documentary, Ifeoluwa , follows Cuppy back to Lagos, the city that shaped her and remains close to her heart. It is also a place connected to some of her greatest successes and deepest heartbreak. The title Ifeoluwa means “The Love of God”. Rather than marking the occasion with another glamorous birthday celebration, Cuppy has chosen to share a more reflective portrait of her life. The film explores womanhood, ambition, identity, belonging and the ongoing process of becoming. There are tender moments, too. Viewers see Cuppy not just as a public figure, but as a daughter, sister and granddaughter. Her time with her grandmother offers an especially intimate glimpse into the affection and family ties at the heart of her story. The documentary also captures an evolution audiences may already have noticed. Her signature pink hair has given way to a new look, while faith, education and service have become increasingly central to how Cuppy speaks about her future. This is not a rejection of music, but a fuller picture of the person behind it. Her philanthropic work remains an important part of that picture. Through the Cuppy Foundation, she has helped raise more than $17 million to support displaced children in Nigeria, in partnership with Save the Children. She has also established education funds at the University of Oxford, New York University and King’s College London to help students overcome financial barriers, particularly those from Africa. Alongside this work, Cuppy remains active as an international DJ, with performances at Glastonbury, Wireless Festival and Cannes Lions, as well as events during United Nations General Assembly week. At its heart, Ifeoluwa is a personal homecoming that brings together family, faith, Lagos and the experiences shaping Cuppy’s next chapter. Guided by the theme “ Behind the Beat, Beyond the Beat ”, this year’s nominations span music production, songwriting, sound engineering, music video direction, broadcasting, digital music platforms, artist management and the wider business of music. The awards spotlight the people and teams whose contributions often happen beyond the public gaze but remain essential to the creation, distribution and commercial success of music. The production categories feature leading and emerging talents across Afro Pop, Afro Beat, Afro R&B, Afro Hip-Hop, Afro Highlife, Afro Soul, Afro Dancehall and Afro Gospel. Nominees include Magicsticks, Sarz, Niphkeys, Ozedikus, Fresh VDM, Ragee, Saszy Afroshii, Tems, Dunnie, Bloody Civilian and rising producers Hunkie Beats, Juixce, Decs, Lekaa Beats, JJAY, Jhay2unez and Shallythechampion. The 2026 field also recognises technical and creative excellence in mixing and mastering, music video direction and songwriting. Broadcasting, media and music business categories include radio and television stations, OAPs, DJs, artist managers, record labels, blogs, online music platforms, A&Rs, live bands and entertainment lawyers. “ Behind every hit record is a team the audience never sees. Our nominees are the engine of African music.” — Elijah John , Founder & Executive Producer, The Beatz Awards Public voting opens on 21 October and runs until 16 November 2026. Music fans and supporters are encouraged to visit the official website, explore the nominees and cast their votes. The 11th Edition awards ceremony will take place on 21 November 2026 at Shell Hall, MUSON Centre, Onikan, Lagos. entertainment.description: Achraf Hakimi with his trophy after winning African Player of the Year at the 2025 CAF Awards. Photo Credit: CAF/Instagram For the first time in 12 years, Lagos will host the CAF Awards, with the 2026 ceremony scheduled for Wednesday, 2 December. The event, which was originally set for 7 December, will bring together leading African footballers, coaches and teams at the Professor Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and the Arts in Iganmu. Spanning 18 award categories across men’s and women’s football, the 2026 CAF Awards will celebrate the finest players, coaches, national teams, and clubs across the continent while bringing football royalty, Nollywood stars, Afrobeats performers, and fashion insiders together on one red carpet. The 2026 shortlists come with a notable twist for the host nation. No Nigerian player made the ten-man shortlist for the CAF Men’s Player of the Year award—leaving out Super Eagles stars Victor Osimhen and Ademola Lookman alongside Egypt’s Mohamed Salah —and no Nigerian footballer features in the CAF Women’s Player of the Year category either, with three-time Women’s Goalkeeper of the Year winner Chiamaka Nnadozie also absent from the final lists. Chiamaka Nnadozie celebrating her third consecutive Goalkeeper of the Year win at the 2025 CAF Awards. Photo Credit: Chiamaka Nnadozie/Instagram Even so, Nigeria still has four nominations to look forward to on home soil on 2 December. The Super Falcons are nominated for Women’s National Team of the Year alongside Algeria, Cabo Verde, Cameroon, Côte d’Ivoire, Ghana, Malawi, Mali, Morocco, and South Africa. In the individual women’s categories, Edo Queens and Falconets shot-stopper Christiana Uzoma represents Nigeria on the Women’s Goalkeeper of the Year shortlist, while Nigerian youth internationals Seimeyeha Janet Akekoromowei and Oluwakemi Adegbuyi are both in the running for Women’s Young Player of the Year. Elsewhere, the headline races feature some of the biggest names in global football. Defending winner Achraf Hakimi of Morocco and Paris Saint-Germain leads the CAF Men’s Player of the Year nominees alongside his compatriots Brahim Diaz and Ismael Saibari , Senegal’s Sadio Mané , Ismaila Sarr , and Pape Gueye , Côte d’Ivoire’s Amad Diallo , Ghana’s Antoine Semenyo , DR Congo’s Yoane Wissa , and South Africa’s Teboho Mokoena . Ademola Lookman celebrating his Men’s Player of the Year victory at the 2024 CAF Awards. entertainment.title: Celebrating 50 Years of Nourishment: Maltina Introduces Its New Look to Trade Partners
entertainment.description: Maltina has unveiled its refreshed visual identity at a trade launch event in Lagos, marking 50 years of nourishing Nigerian homes and introducing a new look for the iconic malt brand while retaining the taste and nutritional qualities consumers have come to love. Held on Friday, November 6, 2026, at the Balmoral Convention Centre, Ikeja, the event brought together business partners, distributors, consumers and other distinguished guests to celebrate the milestone and experience the refreshed brand through interactive activities, entertainment and product showcases. First introduced as Maltona in 1976 and renamed Maltina in 1977, the brand has maintained a strong presence in Nigerian homes for over five decades. Its journey has been defined by a commitment to nourishment, including its introduction of multivitamin enrichment in 1993 and calcium fortification in 2009. Beyond its product innovations, Maltina continues to build meaningful connections with consumers through initiatives such as Maltina Nourishment Tour, Maltina Dance All, Maltina Teacher of the Year (MTOTY), and its Christmas and Ramadan festive campaigns, creating opportunities for learning, participation and shared experiences. Speaking at the event, Sarah Agha , Marketing Director, Nigerian Breweries Plc., reflected on the brand’s journey and the thinking behind its refreshed identity. She highlighted Maltina’s longstanding commitment to nourishment and happiness, noting that the new look represents a more contemporary and confident expression of the brand as it prepares for its next chapter. The refreshed packaging features an enriched signature orange, gold accents and barley elements that reinforce Maltina’s malt credentials. The updated sunrays represent vitality and optimism, while the more prominent calcium coin highlights its nourishment proposition. The gold crown cork and the addition of ‘Since 1976’ further celebrate the brand’s heritage. She reassured consumers that while the brand’s visual identity has evolved, its familiar taste and nutritional credentials remain unchanged. She said “This is not just about refreshing our identity; it is about reaffirming our commitment to nourishment and to families across Nigeria. Our new look makes these commitments even more visible. While our identity has evolved to welcome a new chapter, our taste and nutritional credentials remain unchanged. It is still New Look, Same Nourishing Taste,” In his welcome address, Thibaut Boidin , Managing Director, Nigerian Breweries Plc., celebrated Maltina’s remarkable journey and acknowledged the consumers, partners and distributors whose continued support has contributed to the brand’s growth. He also reiterated the company’s commitment to social impact, announcing plans to support the education of children from underserved communities in the coming year. entertainment.title: How to Style a Pink Buba With a Mini Skirt: Alex Unusual’s Loving Itohan Look
entertainment.description: Alex Unusual’s gold grillz, crystal floral choker, and cherub-accented sunglasses. Who says a buba has to be paired with a wrapper? Nigerian actress, media personality, and reality television star Asogwa Alexandra A —popularly known as Alex Unusua l—is giving us another way to wear the traditional Yoruba top, and her look for the premiere of Loving Itohan makes a strong case for pairing it with a mini skirt. The actress chose a bright fuchsia satin buba with wide half-sleeves, styling it with a fitted mini skirt made from emerald-green and magenta floral brocade damask . It’s an interesting way to rethink the familiar iro and bubacombination: keep the traditional top, swap the wrapper for a shorter skirt, and let the difference in fabric and colour give the outfit its character. The smooth finish of the pink satin against the patterned damask also shows how to wear two statement fabrics without making them compete . The trick is to give each piece a clear role, with the pink buba providing a bold block of colour and the brocade bringing in pattern and texture. Alex Unusual puts a modern spin on the Yoruba iro and buba with a satin top and brocade mini skirt. The mini skirt also gives the outfit a contemporary take on the Oleku silhouette, which traditionally pairs a loose or fitted buba with a wrapper tied above the knee. Alex’s version plays with that familiar proportion, using a fitted damask skirt in place of the wrapper. If you are wondering how to wear a buba and mini skirt without the proportions feeling off, the secret is balancing volume with structure. Because a traditional buba comes with a relaxed cut and wide sleeves, tucking it cleanly into a fitted, high-waisted mini skirt defines the waist and keeps the silhouette neat rather than boxy. Mixing textures intentionally helps too—pairing a plain silk, satin, or AsoOke top with a patterned damask, jacquard, or beaded mini skirt lets both pieces complement each other rather than clash. An oversized gold lip-shaped brooch secured one side, adding another detail to the headpiece. Using the same fabric for the skirt and gele also helped bring the different parts of the outfit together, while keeping the pink buba at the centre of the colour story. entertainment.description: Kerrygold strengthened its engagement with consumers and showcased its distinctive dairy offerings at the 25th Women in Management, Business and Public Service (WIMBIZ) Annual Conference, held on November 5 and 6, 2026, at Eko Hotel & Suites, Lagos. The participation provided an opportunity for the renowned Irish dairy brand to connect with an influential audience of women in business, leadership and public service. Through its sponsorship of the conference, Kerrygold aligned with a platform that brings together accomplished women from diverse sectors to share ideas, build networks and explore opportunities for growth. The 25th edition, which celebrated WIMBIZ’s 25-year contribution to women’s empowerment, was themed “ Rooted, Rising, Ready: Born in Africa, Built for the World,” with conversations centred on leadership, business growth and the evolving role of African women in shaping the future. A key highlight of Kerrygold’s participation was its exhibition stand, where attendees had the opportunity to explore the brand’s product range, learn more about its dairy offerings and enjoy product sampling. The stand also provided a welcoming space for direct interactions with guests, allowing them to experience Kerrygold more closely and discover what makes its products distinctive. Beyond showcasing its products, Kerrygold’s presence at the conference reflected its commitment to strengthening brand visibility, building relevance and fostering meaningful consumer relationships. By creating opportunities for attendees to interact with the brand and experience its offerings firsthand, Kerrygold brought its quality and distinctive taste closer to an audience with whom it sought to build lasting connections. As Kerrygold continues to grow its presence in Nigeria, engagements at relevant platforms such as WIMBIZ complement its efforts to introduce more consumers to the brand. Rooted in a rich Irish dairy heritage and celebrated for its distinctive rich, creamy taste, Kerrygold remains focused on creating opportunities for more people to discover and enjoy its quality dairy products. entertainment.title: Olumide Oworu Declares House of Representatives Bid for Surulere Constituency 1 in 2027
entertainment.description: Olumide Oworu has declared his candidacy for the Federal House of Representatives to represent Surulere Constituency 1 in 2027. Photo Credit: Olumide Oworu/Instagram Actor and media personality Olumide Oworu has declared his intention to contest for the Federal House of Representatives seat for Surulere Constituency 1 in the 2027 general elections. He will be running under the platform of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM). Olumide, who grew up in Surulere, Lagos, has a long-standing connection to the constituency. He began his acting career as a child, appearing in television productions such as Everyday People , before gaining wider recognition for his role in The Johnsons and other Nigerian film and television projects. This is his second attempt to enter legislative politics. In 2023, he declared his intention to contest for a seat in the Lagos State House of Assembly under the Labour Party. However, administrative challenges prevented his name from appearing on the final ballot. Olumide Oworu’s official campaign poster for the House of Representatives seat representing Surulere Constituency 1 under the Allied Peoples Movement. Photo Credit: Olumide Oworu/Instagram Reflecting on that experience in his candidacy announcement on Instagram, Olumide said the support he received from young people in Surulere had strengthened his belief in their readiness for more active participation in governance. “Despite the administrative hurdles that left our names off the final ballot, your resilience showed me that our vision was never a passing phase. Instead, it was the beginning of something much more significant,” he wrote. Explaining his decision to contest again, this time for a seat in the House of Representatives, he added: “We cannot afford to sit on the sidelines while our future is decided by a political class that won’t have to live with the consequences of today’s choices.” His campaign has highlighted issues including gaps in public services, community infrastructure and the participation of young Nigerians in policy decisions. Announcing his candidacy, he said he looked forward to continued support as he and his supporters worked towards what he described as a mission to “Reset Nigeria”. Olumide Oworu is contesting for a legislative seat in Surulere Constituency 1 under the APM platform. entertainment.title: Seven New Tracks From Rema? E-Mortal Boy (EMB) Is Coming Next Week
entertainment.description: Rema announces his upcoming 7-track EP, E-Mortal Boy (EMB), scheduled for release on 20 November 2026. Photo Credit: Rema/Instagram Rema is getting ready to give fans a fresh body of music! The Nigerian singer has officially announced that his new seven-track EP, E-Mortal Boy ( EMB ), will be released next Friday, 20 November 2026. It’s been a little while since his last EP, so there’s plenty of reason for fans to be curious about what he has been working on. The 26-year-old Benin City star first introduced himself to listeners with his self-titled debut EP in 2019, released under Mavin Records and Jonzing World. Since then, he’s built an impressive catalogue, moving between different sounds while taking his music to audiences around the world. His 2022 debut album, Rave & Roses, marked a major turning point in his career, followed by the return to a more raw Afrobeats sound on the 2023 EP Ravage. In 2024, he switched things up again with HEIS , his high-intensity sophomore album, which earned him further international attention. Rema preparing for the release of his new EP E-Mortal Boy following his singles TEA and Oh No. Photo Credit: Rema/Instagram Now, Rema is opening another chapter with E-Mortal Boy (EMB). The project already has two singles to introduce its sound: “ Oh No ” and the fan-favourite “ TEA “. Both tracks give listeners an early taste of the music surrounding the new release, although Rema is keeping the rest of the project under wraps for now. The full tracklist and details of any featured artists have yet to be revealed. With seven tracks, E-Mortal Boy (EMB) will be Rema’s first EP since Ravage and his latest project following HEIS . The singer is set to release it on digital streaming platforms on 20 November, giving fans a new collection to get into as he continues to build on an already eventful musical journey. entertainment.title: Awar Odhiang Named Model of the Year at The Fashion Awards 2026
entertainment.description: Awar Odhiang featured in Vogue wearing a floral printed dress and sculpted oversized rose headpiece. Photo Credit: Awar Odhiang/Instagram Remember the model who turned the finale of Matthieu Blazy ‘s first Chanel show into one of the most talked-about runway moments of 2025? That was Awar Odhiang, and she has another major reason to celebrate. The South Sudanese-Canadian model has been named Model of the Year at The Fashion Awards 2026. The 25-year-old will receive the honour at London’s Royal Albert Hall on 30 November. Born in a refugee camp in Ethiopia and raised in Canada, Awar’s journey to the international fashion scene has taken her from being discovered in Alberta to walking some of the world’s biggest runways. She is now represented by major modelling agencies across London, Milan, Paris and New York. Awar Odhiang walking the red carpet at the 2026 Met Gala in New York City. Photo Credit: Awar Odhiang/Instagram Her runway résumé includes shows for Prada, Versace, Miu Miu, Saint Laurent and Jacquemus, but it was her appearance at Chanel’s Spring/Summer 2026 show in October 2025 that introduced her to an even wider audience. Closing Matthieu Blazy’s first collection for the fashion house, Awar wore the show’s bridal look, featuring an oversized white shirt and a voluminous, colourful feathered skirt. But it was what happened at the finale that captured everyone’s attention. As the models gathered for their final walk, Awar broke formation, smiling, clapping and twirling in her skirt. When Blazy appeared, she ran towards him and embraced him. The spontaneous moment quickly went viral, with fashion fans celebrating the joy she brought to the runway. It was also a historic appearance: Awar became only the third Black woman to close a Chanel show in the house’s 115-year history, after Alek Wek and Adut Akech. Model of the Year 2026 winner Awar Odhiang backstage at the Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show. Photo Credit: Awar Odhiang/Instagram Since then, her career has continued to gather pace. Awar has appeared on eight international magazine covers this year and fronted campaigns for Chanel, Chloé, Louis Vuitton, Saint Laurent, Loro Piana and H&M. She has also used her growing platform to speak up for greater representation and inclusion of Black models in the luxury fashion industry. Awar Odhiang in Daniel Roseberry’s Schiaparelli Spring 2026 Haute Couture collection in Paris. Photo Credit: Awar Odhiang/Instagram Her Model of the Year recognition celebrates a remarkable year of runway, editorial and campaign work, as well as the influence she continues to have beyond the catwalk. On 30 November, she’ll take that recognition to the Royal Albert Hall, adding another milestone to a career that is still unfolding. entertainment.description: The Francophone African Music Industries Fair (SIMA) announces the third edition of the event, taking place on November 12–13, 2026, in Cotonou, Republic of Benin. Following its previous edition, which brought together more than 6,700 participants and over 3,000 industry professionals, this pan-African gathering dedicated to the cultural and creative industries returns with a clear ambition: African Music: From the Stage to Global Influence. SIMA 2026 is supported by major institutional and private-sector partners, including the Ministry of Culture, Arts and Heritage of Benin,the Ministry of Tourism and Foreign Trade of Benin,the Embassy of France in Côte d’Ivoire,the BOAD Foundation, as well as SACEM, Sony Music and Warner Music Africa. These partnerships reflect the growing interest in the development and structuring of Africa’s cultural and creative industries. For the second consecutive year, Benin will host SIMA, in line with the country’s broader efforts to strengthen the role of the cultural and creative industries in the structural transformation of its economy and to enhance its cultural influence at both regional and international levels. Co-founded in 2022 by cultural entrepreneur Mamby Diomandé and artist and producer Pit Baccardi , SIMA has established itself as a platform dedicated to structuring, connecting and developing Africa’s creative ecosystems. By placing music at the heart of a broader reflection on the transformation of culture and the creative industries, SIMA also seeks to address the technological shifts reshaping the sector—from artificial intelligence to new ways of creating, distributing and consuming content. entertainment.title: Ayra Starr Joins Coachella 2027 Lineup Alongside SZA, Dua Lipa & More
entertainment.description: Ayra Starr returns with her third studio album, Starrgirl. Ayra Starr is taking her global run to another big stage! The Nigerian singer has been named among the performers at Coachella 2027, adding another major festival appearance to her growing list of international milestones. The Beninese-born singer, who rose to prominence as one of Afrobeats’ leading voices after joining Mavin Records, is set to perform on both weekends of the festival, Sunday, April 11, and Sunday, April 18, 2027. Coachella will take place at the Empire Polo Club in Indio, California. It’s been a big year for Ayra, with her third studio album, Starrgirl, adding to an already exciting run. Fans heading to the festival can look forward to hearing songs from the project, including “ Tornado ” and “ Midnight in New York “, as well as her collaboration “ Gimme Dat “. There’s also room for crowd favourites such as “ Rush “, “ Commas ” and “ Heaven Baby “. Ayra shares the Sunday bill with headliner SZA , alongside Victoria Monét , Jorja Smith , Becky G and Don Toliver . The wider festival, running from April 9 to 11 and April 16 to 18, will also feature headliners Dua Lipa and Tame Impala , with Madonna set for a special appearance in the dance tent. Her Coachella booking follows another major moment in London, where she performed at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium as part of the NFL International Games halftime show, becoming the first African artist to headline the show. And there’s even more for fans to look forward to. Ayra has announced her 20-city Starrgirl World Tour , which will take her across Europe and North America in early 2027 before she heads to the California desert for Coachella. What a year ahead for the Starr girl. entertainment.title: Meagan Good & Jonathan Majors Look Picture-Perfect at AFRIFF in Lagos
entertainment.description: Meagan Good and Jonathan Majors coordinating in neutral tones and a red cap accent for AFRIFF. Who knew an ivory mini dress and a classic black suit could make such an interesting pairing? During their time in Lagos for AFRIFF, Meagan Good and Jonathan Majors posed for a studio portrait in two looks that took very different approaches to dressing up. Meagan’s dress brought together colourful beadwork, a fitted silhouette and a floor-length train, while Jonathan opted for black tailoring, an open-neck white shirt and a red cap. And while his outfit keeps things relatively simple, there’s nothing ordinary about the details of hers. Let’s start with Meagan’s dress, because there is quite a lot happening here. At first glance, the ivory mini might seem relatively simple, but look a little closer and the details begin to unfold. The fitted halter-neck bodice is covered in rows of turquoise, bronze and dark green beads, arranged horizontally to follow the shape of her waist. Then there’s the skirt, which takes a more unexpected turn with clusters of dark beaded embellishments scattered across the fabric. And just when you think you’ve taken it all in, an extended panel falls from the side of the mini skirt, creating a long, floor-sweeping train. It’s a fun combination of short and dramatic, with the beadwork giving the dress plenty to say without needing much else. Meagan Good styled in a sculpted halter-neck corset dress featuring multi-coloured beaded detailing and a side train. Meagan kept the rest of her styling fairly simple. Black ankle-strap heels and a textured black clutch were her accessories of choice, while her voluminous curls were left loose around her shoulders. Her bronze-toned makeup and glossy nude lip tied everything together without competing with the dress. Jonathan went in a completely different direction, keeping things classic with a black jacket and matching trousers over a white shirt, worn open at the neck. A grey patterned scarf added another detail around the collar, while his light-framed sunglasses and black patent shoes completed the outfit. But it’s the red cap that really changes the look. Against all that black and white, it gives the outfit a welcome hit of colour and makes the styling feel more personal. Meagan Good and Jonathan Majors showcasing intricate beaded dress embroidery and red cap styling. It’s an interesting pairing: Meagan’s dress has all the beadwork, colour and movement, while Jonathan’s outfit is built around simple tailoring and a few well-chosen accessories. There’s plenty to appreciate in both, wouldn’t you agree? sports.title: Cowboys Skip Deadline Splashes To Bet On Existing Talent
sports.description: Robert Goddin-Imagn Images The Dallas Cowboys stayed quiet at the trade deadline. While other teams scrambled for last-minute upgrades, Dallas decided to trust the players already in the building. ESPN insider Adam Schefter noted that the organization never appeared close to making another major deal. “It never sounded like they got close to making any big deals,” Schefter said, adding that there was no real movement on a George Pickens trade. This approach puts the pressure squarely on the current squad to deliver results over the final eight games. Why The Roster Stays Put General Manager Jerry Jones and the front office clearly believe they have enough pieces to win. They already spent a 2028 second-round pick earlier in the season to add cornerback Joey Porter Jr. from the Pittsburgh Steelers. That move gave the secondary a physical presence without burning up all their draft capital. The team said the addition was an aggressive upgrade to the roster. “Rather than surrender more draft capital, the organization will give its existing players an opportunity to deliver,” the report states. sports.title: England's Mitchell could miss Six Nations after hamstring operation
sports.description: Mitchell's four hamstring injuries this year have not all been on the same leg, with three to his right and one to his left [Getty Images] England scrum-half Alex Mitchell could miss next year's Six Nations after an operation to fix recurring hamstring issues. The 29-year-old, who was Steve Borthwick's first-choice nine last season, has gone under the knife after suffering four hamstring injuries this year. If Mitchell, who has recovered ahead of schedule in the past, follows an estimated four-month rehabilitation it would give him a chance of playing in England's final two matches, against Wales and Scotland on 6 and 13 March. Any setback however would leave him with only pre-tournament friendlies to play in for England before next year's Rugby World Cup in Australia. Mitchell's latest hamstring injury, which came in Northampton's win over Gloucester last month, ruled him out of this month's Nations Championship campaign. Mitchell suffered an injury to the same hamstring against Ireland in February and again against Fiji in July. He also tweaked his other hamstring - his left, non-kicking leg - in an England training camp in May. Mitchell told the i Paper last month that he had been given the option, like skipper Maro Itoje, to skip England's summer fixtures against South Africa, Fiji and Argentina, but opted to play instead. While Jack van Poortvliet has emerged as Borthwick's starting pick in Mitchell's absence, there is competition behind the Leicester man with Bristol's Harry Randall, Bath's Ben Spencer and Mitchell's club team-mate Archie McParland all vying for position. Mitchell travelled to Finland to be operated on by Lasse Lempainen, a specialist in elite sporting injuries. Chelsea and England defender Reece James and Paris St-Germain's Ballon D'Or winner Ousmane Dembele are among Lempainen's previous patients, both returning to consistent playing time after a string of muscular injuries. Mitchell's England team-mate Ben Curry was also operated on by Lempainen and has made a successful return to action after 10 months out, featuring in England's win over Australia last weekend. sports.description: Jordan Ayew joined Championship side Sheffield United in September after spending two seasons with Leicester City [Getty Images] Ghana belatedly kick-started their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) qualifying campaign with a 2-0 home win over Somalia. The Black Stars had lost their opening two Group C matches against Ivory Coast and The Gambia, leading to the departure of coach Carlos Queiroz by mutual consent. Ghana women's coach Kim Bjorkegren was placed in interim charge for this month's double-header against the Ocean Stars, with the West Africans in danger of missing a second successive edition of the Afcon finals. The hosts were given a chance to take an early lead in Sekondi-Takoradi after Alidu Seidu was pulled down in the box, but Jordan Ayew's 14th-minute penalty was saved by Somalia goalkeeper Ibrahim Hussein. Ghana did go ahead in first-half stoppage time when Mohammed Salisu headed Mohammed Kudus's deep corner back across goal and Jonas Adjetey nodded in from six yards out. Felix Afena-Gyan doubled the Black Stars' advantage just after the hour mark when his shot from inside the box squirmed under Hussein and over the line. The result puts the four-time continental champions three points behind Ivory Coast and The Gambia, who meet in Bouake at 19:00 GMT. Cameroon, DR Congo and Senegal are also in action among seven other Afcon 2027 qualifiers on Thursday.

sports.title: Alysa Liu speaks on new winning mentality in Life magazine cover story
sports.description: This winter, Alysa Liu was the name on everyone's lips. The skating star, who hails from Oakland, wowed audiences around the world when she won the individual gold medal at the 2026 Winter Olympics in Milan . She also won the group gold with Team USA. The then-20-year-old captured attention with her confidence in her individuality, including a striped hairstyle and a "smiley" piercing. She is now taking a break and is not competing in the 2026-27 season , but promises "I have a plan" in her cover story for LIFE Magazine that was published online Thursday, Nov. 12. The publication will return to print on Nov. 23, which is 90 years after its first issue. The comeback arrives after a nearly 20-year hiatus. Liu is the first of five cover stars that will be featured on the first edition of the re-upped quarterly magazine. The story, written by Bonnie Tsui, is accompanied by striking photographs by Spike Jonze of Liu skating in a flowing red outfit in a darkened rink. The feature reflects on Liu's previous time stepping away from the sport during the COVID pandemic. She realized that she wasn't skating for herself, but to please others. "When I was younger, I wanted to win all the time," she said. "But winning was really about getting reassurance from my coach and my dad, and just making them happy, making them think I was, like, perfect or something." In the piece, Liu shows the many sides of her life after fame. She trains at the Yerba Buena Ice Skating & Bowling Center in San Francisco, carefully crafting her next routines with her coaches Phillip DiGuglielmo and Massimo Scali. She has a lunch full of laughs at A16, a pizzeria in Oakland, with her closest friends. Liu explained how her perspective in being open with the world has changed since rising to superstardom. She's not only become a sports icon, but has become a well-known name is fashion, attending the Met Gala and Paris Fashion Week. "I don’t really like hiding stuff about myself," she said. "But now, I low-key have to, to protect my peace." She pondered how taking ownership of her sport allowed her to travel with her siblings and makes her excited to support her United States teammates from the stands, emphasizing how she values camaraderie. Liu said at the peak of her unhappiness she "would cry all the time – like, every session – and not in a good way." But she has no regrets. "If I went back in time, I would still want myself to go through everything, just so I could come to my own conclusion," she said. "Now, I don’t look to other people to find my happiness anymore. That has changed the definition of winning for me." Fans can pre-order their copy of LIFE Magazine featuring Liu online or purchase a magazine at select retailers on Nov. 23. sports.title: CJ McCollum joins NBA on Prime crew, discusses role on Hawks, Damian Lillard's comeback
sports.description: CJ McCollum hit the game-winning shot in the Atlanta Hawks ' Game 3 victory over the New York Knicks in the first round of last year's playoffs. Not only does he remember that shot, but he remembers enjoying being a guest on Prime Video's "NBA Nightcap" postgame show where he appeared in his pajamas and the hosts joked he put the Knicks "to sleep." They all laughed about his role of villain as his son popped in to say hello. The party doesn't have to stop there as NBA on Prime announced on Thursday, Nov. 12 that the 14-year veteran guard will be a player commentator for several programs this season starting with "NBA Nightcap" on Friday, Nov. 13. "The conversation and team analysis that night was really fun," he told USA TODAY Sports of the postgame memories, "and I thought the chemistry was there, and I felt like it made a lot of sense (for me to join the Prime team). And I have a great appreciation for what NBA on Prime is doing, what the crew is doing, and how they educate and share authentic analysis." McCollum, 35, majored in journalism at Lehigh University and has experience hosting his own podcast with "The CJ McCollum Show" and "Pull Up with CJ McCollum." Among Prime's All-Star team of talent that he is joining is a mix of longtime broadcasters, including Kevin Harlan, and basketball greats like Udonis Haslem, Dirk Nowitzki, Steve Nash and Candace Parker. McCollum said the team is "a really cool atmosphere, really great environment of people that I respect and admire." "They're very honest. They watch the game. They're students of the game. They’re people who appreciate the game and they do a great job of describing why certain things are happening," he continued. "... When you have that group of professionals who have played the game, have talked the game, have lived the game, have been around it and seen it for so long, you get various impactful moments where viewers are able to really get a glimpse of what's actually happening, why it's happening, in an insightful way that they can digest." McCollum appreciates the craft of journalism and how showing the human element of any story brings people together. As journalism continues to face industry challenges , the 2016 Most Improved Player has hope. "Storytelling is vital. I think it makes the world a better place," he said. "Being able to hear people's stories, being able to see people's journeys not just in the sports world but in life, I think is something that we all can appreciate. "And journalism isn't dying. It's just evolving. But I think the people who move with integrity, who do things the right way and really appreciate the craft are continuing to thrive for sure." sports.title: CJ McCollum Is Still in the NBA — Why Is He Taking a TV Analyst Job?
sports.description: CJ McCollum - CJ McCollum (Paras Griffin/Getty Images) CJ McCollum might still be hitting key shots for the Atlanta Hawks on the court, but the 13-year NBA veteran is adding another major media gig to his resume. Prime Video announced that McCollum is joining the NBA on Prime broadcast team as a player contributor for the 2026–27 season. The former National Basketball Players Association (NBPA) president will make select studio appearances throughout the year, kicking off his run on NBA Nightcap following Friday’s Emirates NBA Cup slate, which features a game between the New York Knicks and Indiana Pacers. The 35-year-old athlete isn’t a stranger to balancing both worlds. With a journalism degree from Lehigh University and a history of digital media ventures—including hosting and executive producing his ReMaking America talk show on PlayersTV—he has long prepared for life outside the court. “So much has changed about how fans experience the game, and I’m excited to join Prime Video to share something only a player can: what’s really going on in the locker room, on the floor, and in the league right now,” McCollum said in a statement. “I’m still a player first, but this was too good an opportunity to pass up.” Prime Video leadership is equally enthusiastic about what his perspective as an active player can bring to their second season of coverage. “We’re thrilled to have CJ join NBA on Prime,” Amina Hussein, Prime Video Head of On-Air Talent and Development, also said in the statement. “As a 13-year veteran and former NBPA president, he brings a unique insight that our viewers want to hear. His ability to connect with fans and give his perspective on a specific play, or the reason behind a certain outcome, makes him a perfect fit for our second season of NBA on Prime.” Related Fans Compare ABC’s New Shaquille O’Neal Hide-and-Seek Show to a '30 Rock' Joke McCollum certainly has the resume to back it up. He was named the NBA’s Most Improved Player in 2016, when he broke out as a dynamic scorer with the Portland Trail Blazers and helped lead the franchise to the 2019 Western Conference Finals. Over a career spanning more than a decade, he has amassed over 16,000 points and averaged 20 or more points per game for over 10 consecutive seasons. Having also served as president of the NBPA from 2021 to 2025, McCollum brings a rare administrative and on-court vantage point to the desk. Even as he navigates transitioning to a bench role with the Hawks this season, McCollum follows in the footsteps of other active NBA players like Golden States Warriors forward Draymond Green—who serves as a guest analyst on Inside the NBA and hosts The Draymond Green Show —as well as fellow NBA on Prime contributors Kyle Lowry and Tyrese Haliburton , who have stepped onto the analyst desk while still playing on the court. sports.title: Mark Daigneault provides injury update on Thomas Sorber
sports.description: Habitually going through pregame warmups all of the 2026-27 regular season, Thomas Sorber awaits his NBA debut. The 20-year-old continues to recover from a follow-up knee procedure he had in July. Once viewed as a four-week timetable, it's been four months without being given the green light to go. The Oklahoma City Thunder badly need NBA-capable bodies. As evident in their two losses to the Portland Trail Blazers on their recent back-to-back. Injuries have completely wrecked any championship ambitions. The headliners, of course, are Chet Holmgren, Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace being sidelined for two-plus months — with the latter two possibly being out for the whole year. With how dire the health situation is, all eyes dart over to Sorber — who has been out of action for a year and a half. When can the Thunder expect him to be a frontcourt reinforcement? We still don't know the exact answer, but Thunder head coach Mark Daigneault has applauded his grueling recovery process. sports.description: 1979 Toyota Celica 2000GT RA45 Group 4. Image credit: TTTNIS/Wikimedia Commons (CC0) Everyone will write about the badge. Fair enough: the Celica name, which carried Carlos Sainz to world titles in 1990 and 1992, is back on a Rally1 car for 2027. But the nameplate is the least interesting part of Toyota’s announcement. The detail worth your attention is the structure behind it: two teams, two cars, and, by Toyota’s own account, the same power and performance in both. My read: this is less a heritage stunt than a hedge, and a bolder one than it looks. Toyota has put its strongest 2026 drivers behind the new name and left the old one to the comeback cast. That choice tells you where the company expects its pressure, and its proof, to come from. What Toyota actually confirmed On 3 November, TOYOTA GAZOO Racing laid out a 2027 line-up split across two entries that both run out of the team’s Jyväskylä base. GAZOO Racing TOYOTA will run the GR Yaris Rally1 for Ott Tänak and Martin Järveoja, Takamoto Katsuta and Aaron Johnston, and Kalle Rovanperä and Jonne Halttunen on a partial season of selected events. Both cars are built to the new WRC Car regulations. Toyota says they will have equal power and performance, that homologation is due before the end of 2026, and that further details and liveries will follow before the season. Up to six factory cars can start a given rally. Sébastien Ogier may make selected appearances. What the release does not give you is an engine specification, any description of how the two cars differ, or a single word about a road-going Celica. Anything on that last point is speculation. Elfyn Evans, pictured in a GR Yaris Rally1 at the 2023 Central European Rally, moves to the Celica-badged team for 2027. Toyota did not hide its new nameplate behind a development driver or a part-timer. It handed it to the champion and the two men who came closest to beating him. sports.title: I managed Wrexham - Phil Parkinson needs to follow my lead to get best out of his team
sports.description: Wrexham will face Lincoln City after the international break -Credit:GETTY Every manager will have a philosophy, a preferred way of playing and, ideally, a preferred starting eleven. But football has a habit of ripping up even the best-laid plans. Injuries, illness, loss of form, suspensions, attitude and a whole host of other factors can quickly turn a managers carefully constructed blueprint on its head. That is when flexibility, both tactically and within the squad, becomes so important. The past week has been a good example of how a relatively small tactical adjustment can make a significant difference, particularly when a squad is being ravaged by injuries in key attacking areas. With three creative players unavailable, alongside the new long-term injury to Sam Smith (wishing him a speedy recovery), Phil Parkinson has been forced to revisit a familiar formation from our League One campaign. Without our recognised ‘number 10s’, he has returned to a midfield three, with one holding midfielder, or ‘6’, and two more advanced ‘8s’, rather than the previous system of two deeper midfielders and two attacking tens. For me, it brought greater balance. Against Blackburn, Todd Cantwell had found plenty of joy drifting into the wide areas when we were playing with narrow deep midfielders, a number 10 and two strikers. The change helped provide greater defensive stability, but it also offered something going forward. The two ‘8s’ were given more licence to get beyond the ball, link up with the wing-backs and connect with the strikers. It gave us different options and, importantly, a better balance between attack and defence. • All the Phil Parkinson questions you wanted to know but were afraid to ask • Phil Parkinson may need to change his trusted approach to get Wrexham fans back on side Would that change have happened if everyone had been fit? Probably not. And that’s where management becomes interesting. There was another calculated gamble in moving Lewis O’Brien into the number 10 role, playing just off Kieffer Moore. It isn’t a natural position for Lewis, who generally prefers to operate from deeper areas, but he certainly possesses some of the attributes required. His energy allows him to lead the press, he anticipates situations well and his movement can cause opponents problems. It’s a risk when a player hasn’t regularly occupied that position, but Parkinson’s options are limited and sometimes necessity forces your hand. This is where a manager needs a little bit of creative thinking, and perhaps a slice of luck. A new combination clicks, a player discovers a position that suits him or somebody takes an unexpected opportunity and makes it their own. Of course, it doesn’t always work! Brian Flynn and Peter Reid both decided that playing me at right midfield might be the answer at various points in my career. Let’s just say those particular experiments weren’t quite as successful! technology.title: United Airlines wants you to check in, not your chatbot
technology.description: United Airlines has become the latest company to slap restrictions on unauthorized third-party AI agents, warning that the bots could make unintended purchases, expose customer data, or bypass checks requiring human acknowledgment. The airline announced restrictions covering both its own digital platforms and indirect access through travel agencies and aggregators, with changes to its booking, ticketing, and distribution policies. United says automated actions could violate aviation regulations, citing the requirement for a human acknowledgment during check-in that bags contain no banned substances. A bot cheerfully ticking the box isn't quite the passenger confirmation it has in mind. And then there is the worry that "sharing account credentials with personal, third-party, AI assistants can expose sensitive information, and actions taken by these tools may result in unintended purchases, account changes, or use of MileagePlus miles." United would also rather customers use its own app than turn third-party assistants loose on its systems. AI agents are pitched as a way to outsource life's minutiae, and it's difficult to navigate the web without tripping over a breathless influencer explaining why you need one, or dozens, or hundreds of virtual personal assistants. The thing is that operating these assistants requires care and thought. Earlier this year, British mathematician Professor Hannah Fry conducted a cautionary experiment in which she gave an AI agent a bank card, and a bit too much agency, to see what it would do. Passwords were coughed up, and some ill-considered purchases were made. Still, as Fry said of the agent, dubbed Cassandra, "don't let her incompetence fool you, because these things are getting better fast." Last month, reports emerged of major US banks blocking third-party AI agents from operating inside accounts and taking actions on behalf of the customer. This month, several UK banks were reported to have followed suit. United stated: "Corporate leaders in the banking and retail industries have taken similar actions regarding AI agents and we encourage others to consider measures that preserve the data and security of their customers and strengthen safety." The Register asked United Airlines how it planned to implement the blocking. There are a few options, including physical biometric confirmation for actions or checking for signs of automated browser driving. Amazon has also moved against unauthorized AI agents, blocking Meta's Muse (the "AI that gets it done," according to Meta's marketing) in September . The airline has yet to respond. ®

The warning appears in the release documentation for November's Exchange Server SE security update. Looking for Exchange 2016 and 2019 information? Tough. Microsoft stated: "Exchange Server 2016 and 2019 are no longer tested for vulnerabilities and there are no updates released. If you are using those versions of Exchange, you should consider them permanently vulnerable [Microsoft's emphasis] and should upgrade your organization immediately." You have been warned. Support for Exchange Server 2016 and 2019 ended on October 14, 2025, but the company announced an Extended Security Updates (ESU) program in July 2025. The plan was that this program would end on April 14, 2026, by which time customers would surely have made the jump to a later or online version, right? The company said: "This period will not be extended past April 2026 (you do not need to ask)." And... of course it was. As April 2026 rolled around, and it became clear that some customers were still stubbornly sticking with the old versions, Microsoft did the equivalent of heaving an exasperated sigh and offered another six months of paid security updates. Those final weeks also brought a separate treat: a Windows Server update breaking Exchange Server . This time it was serious. Microsoft released the final Exchange Server 2016 and 2019 security updates on October 13. No more patches, no more vulnerability testing, and apparently no more reprieves. According to Microsoft's Security Update Guide , the November update fixed nine vulnerabilities in Exchange Server SE, including a critical remote code execution flaw, CVE-2026-118207. technology.title: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia chief executive

In a Form 8-K [PDF] filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), the GPU maker disclosed that it accepted the resignation of Huang, whom it identified as Jen-Hsun Huang, on November 11, effective immediately. He is being replaced by chief financial officer Colette Kress, who will serve as interim leader while the board conducts a search for a new CEO. Huang, who founded Nvidia in 1993 and served as president, CEO, and a member of the board of directors ever since, led the GPU maker to become one of the most valuable companies in the world, hitting a hit peak of over $5.5 trillion earlier this year. His position became untenable following an investigation by the company's board after he admitted to an affair, amid allegations he had a romantic relationship with a woman the US authorities suspected as a Chinese spy. Reports later surfaced this week of a second alleged affair with an employee of the company itself, reported by the New York Times as being with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of health care. According to the New York Times , US intelligence had reason to believe the woman, Alice Huang, was recruited to gather information about Nvidia and its operations for the Beijing government. Megaspeed also faces claims it was illicitly shipping Nvidia products to China, in violation of US export controls. Any relationship between Huang and a Chinese operative would be enormously concerning, as the US has been trying to keep advanced technology for AI out of the hands of the country, allegedly for security reasons, fearing it might be used for military purposes. For its part, Beijing rejects the spying allegations, saying they are part of a smear campaign against China. Shortly after Nvidia’s board announced it was investigating Huang, he sent an email to Nvidia staff apologizing and confessing to having an affair, though he did not explicitly name Alice Huang in his public apology. It seemed like the leather-jacketed leader might just hang on, since it was difficult to imagine anyone other than him leading the company after all this time. But Nvidia’s shares fell 4.3 percent on November 9 and a further 5.5 percent the following day, wiping around $430 billion off its market value, amid all the speculation. Named simply Arcade , it is a collection of browser games based on classic titles such as Flappy Bird, Snake, and Tetris, but re-tuned as flagrant works of political propaganda. Designed to court reactionary gamers, they push the administration’s policies on immigration and other hot-button issues, while dehumanising their targets. There have recently been some new additions: a Temple Run clone named Red Scare about crossing the “ration market” and escaping the Democratic Socialists of America, and another simple item-matching game about the threat of socialism. In the midst of increasing fuel, utility and grocery prices thanks to the Iran war, these were naked attempts to distract voters by appealing to their video game nostalgia. After an explosion of news coverage, Arcade caught the attention of the games industry. The Tetris Company warned on social media that it “took copyright infringement very seriously.” Days later, the game was removed from the White House site. However, aside from a March 2026 statement from the Pokémon Company condemning the White House for using its characters in Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) propaganda, major video game companies have been relatively silent in the face of the administration’s widespread usage of their IP.
